title: Respond instead of react: calm, anger, grief and bouncing back

say: Respond instead of react: calm, anger, grief and bouncing back.
This is the video for module two of Emotional Intelligence for Daily Life.
A reaction is fast and automatic: a shout, a slammed door. A response is chosen.
For example, Chioma, a civil servant in Enugu, gets a call at work. Her son's fees are overdue. Her face goes hot and she wants to call her husband and shout.

panel.heading: STOP: Chioma gets the school fees call
items: Stop: phone face down, no dialling
Take a breath: one minute of slow breathing
Observe: I am scared and embarrassed
Proceed: call the bursar, then her husband

say: She uses STOP. Stop: she puts the phone face down and does not dial.

say: Take a breath: about one minute of slow breathing at her desk.

say: Observe: I am scared and embarrassed, and I am telling myself he forgot on purpose.

say: Proceed: she calls the bursar and arranges to pay half today and the rest within two weeks. Then she calls her husband calmly to plan together.
Her son stays in school, and the evening is a planning talk instead of a fight.

say: Here is box breathing. Breathe in slowly through your nose for a count of 4.

panel.heading: Calm your body in one minute
items: Breathe in through your nose for 4
Hold gently for 4
Breathe out through your mouth for 4
Hold empty for 4, and repeat 4 times

say: Hold your breath gently for 4.

panel.heading: Calm your body in one minute
items: Breathe in through your nose for 4
Hold gently for 4
Breathe out through your mouth for 4
Hold empty for 4, and repeat 4 times

say: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 4.

panel.heading: Calm your body in one minute
items: Breathe in through your nose for 4
Hold gently for 4
Breathe out through your mouth for 4
Hold empty for 4, and repeat 4 times

say: Hold empty for 4, and repeat 4 times. If holding feels uncomfortable, skip the holds and just make the out-breath longer. A long out-breath slows the heart.

panel.heading: Calm your body in one minute
items: Breathe in through your nose for 4

Breathe out through your mouth for 4
Hold empty for 4, and repeat 4 times

say: Practise for two minutes each morning when you are calm. Then the tool is ready when stress hits.

say: Anger is a normal signal that something feels unfair. The problem is what we do with it. Anger climbs in steps.
At 1 to 3 you are annoyed. Name it, breathe, and speak early and calmly.

panel.heading: Catch anger low on the ladder
items: 1 to 3, annoyed: name it, speak early
4 to 6, frustrated: STOP, lower your voice
7 to 8, angry: take a time-out now
9 to 10, rage: leave safely, talk later

say: At 4 to 6 your jaw is tight and your voice rises. Use STOP and lower your voice on purpose.

panel.heading: Catch anger low on the ladder
items: 1 to 3, annoyed: name it, speak early
4 to 6, frustrated: STOP, lower your voice
7 to 8, angry: take a time-out now
9 to 10, rage: leave safely, talk later

say: At 7 to 8 your face is hot and your fists are clenched. Take a time-out. Say, I need 20 minutes, let us talk again at 8pm. Then come back as agreed.

panel.heading: Catch anger low on the ladder
items: 1 to 3, annoyed: name it, speak early
4 to 6, frustrated: STOP, lower your voice
7 to 8, angry: take a time-out now
9 to 10, rage: leave safely, talk later

say: At 9 to 10, leave the room safely and talk only when calm.
Then use an I statement. I feel worried when the shop is left unlocked, because we could lose our stock.

say: For example, Zainab, a hairdresser in Abuja, has rent due, two clients who have not paid, and a sick mother. She cannot sleep.
She writes 8 worries on paper. 4 she can act on, so she gives each one a time: call the clients at 9am, the landlord at 11am.

panel.heading: Sort what you can control
left: How I speak to my children

say: The other 4 she cannot control. For those she breathes slowly at night and says, I have done what I can today.
By Thursday one client has paid and the landlord gives her 5 extra days.

panel.heading: Sort what you can control
left: How I speak to my children

say: Some things breathing cannot fix. If you or someone at home is being hit, threatened or controlled, your safety comes first. Go to a safe place, and contact trusted family, the police or an organisation that supports women.

panel.heading: When to get help straight away

cards.d: Being hit, threatened or controlled is not an anger problem. Go somewhere safe and get help.
Low most days for over two weeks, or cannot eat, sleep or care for yourself: see a doctor.
Thoughts of harming yourself? Go to the nearest hospital or tell someone close at once.

say: Sadness after a loss is normal, and grief moves back and forth. But if low mood lasts most days for more than two weeks, or you cannot eat, sleep or care for your children, see a doctor or counsellor.

say: If you have any thoughts of harming yourself, go to the nearest hospital emergency unit or tell someone close to you immediately.

say: Resilience is a set of skills anyone can learn. How you explain a setback affects how fast you recover.
For example, Amaka is turned down for a business loan. She thinks, I am not good at business, nothing works for me, I will never grow.

panel.heading: Amaka reframes a rejected loan
items: Personal: not my failing, a fixable reason
Pervasive: one area, the rest is good
Permanent: 6 months of records, then reapply
Connection: join an ajo as a second route

say: Personal: she asks why. She had no 6-month bank statement showing regular sales. That is fixable.

panel.heading: Amaka reframes a rejected loan
items: Personal: not my failing, a fixable reason
Pervasive: one area, the rest is good
Permanent: 6 months of records, then reapply
Connection: join an ajo as a second route

say: Pervasive: her customers are happy and her sister supports her.

say: Permanent: if she puts all her sales through her account for 6 months, she can reapply.

say: To remember. STOP gives you a gap. Box breathing calms the body. Take a time-out early, and come back. Act on what you control. And when it is serious, put your safety first and get help.

panel.heading: Remember
items: STOP gives you a gap to choose
Box breathing: 4 in, hold, 4 out, hold
Take a time-out at anger level 7 or above
Act on what you control; accept the rest
Safety first; get help when it is serious

say: Now practise box breathing every morning for 7 days, write your own anger ladder, and make your support and resilience plans.
Continue with the lessons below.
